messages.content: What is the freezing point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure, provided in kilopascals (kPa) or atmospheres (atm). Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water freezes at roughly **–2.2 °C**.  

This value comes from the water phase diagram: as the pressure drops below atmospheric pressure, the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the melting/freezing temperature decreases. At the triple point (≈ 6.1 kPa, 0.01 °C) water can exist as ice, liquid, or vapor simultaneously. By 10 kPa the freezing point has shifted to about –2 °C, which is the temperature at which ice and liquid water coexist under those conditions.
